rules.name: Protect live installations
rules.rationale: User: live rooms and furniture stay fixed during routine refresh.

rules.name: Fit the display format
rules.rationale: Whole panels require matching nominal format; waterfall may use a verified cut from a larger slab.

rules.name: Exclude discontinued products
rules.rationale: A discontinued product cannot be proposed for a new installation.

rules.name: Add missing designs first
rules.rationale: User: use scarce movable slots to broaden the range.

rules.name: Reduce repeated finishes
rules.rationale: Repeats can remain for bookmatch or a distinct useful finish/application.

rules.name: Give Hit products prime exposure
rules.rationale: User examples: Oro Noir and Tuscano Burgundy. Visibility tiers need a Merch/site review.

rules.name: Keep color families together
rules.rationale: Group family/temperature and order light to dark. Initial ranks are image-derived suggestions.

rules.name: Minimize disruption
rules.rationale: Prefer a product swap within an existing compatible fixture before moving its frame.

rules.name: Protect the central route
rules.rationale: Illustrative keep-out strip, not an accessibility/building-code dimension. Design must supply verified geometry.

rules.name: Release only complete work packages
rules.rationale: A visual proposal may contain missing data. Ordering/installing must expose and resolve those gaps.

questions.question: Which products are Hit, in which market, and until when?
questions.proposed_answer: Oro Noir and Tuscano Burgundy are Hit examples; add market and effective dates.

questions.question: Which sales metric should influence priority, and over what period?
questions.proposed_answer: Showroom/region sales and margin as a limited secondary input; preserve launch exploration.

questions.question: What is the released SKU, finish, launch date and stock for each proposed new product?
questions.proposed_answer: Confirm Tuscano Burgundy and Architeq candidates before ordering.

questions.question: Which designs and finishes must every APS visit expose?
questions.proposed_answer: Maximize distinct designs in movable displays. Mark must-have designs explicitly.

questions.question: When is a repeat useful, and how many are allowed?
questions.proposed_answer: Retain documented bookmatch; prefer a new finish or format to an exact repeat.

questions.question: Which color groups and order should each family use?
questions.proposed_answer: Draft: family, warm/neutral subgroup, then light to dark. Confirm Architeq and Serena ranks.

questions.question: Which slots count as prime, secondary and commercial exposure?
questions.proposed_answer: Review the proposed map overlay and closed-bank front positions.

questions.question: Who can release changes, with what move/budget limit?
questions.proposed_answer: Merch releases work. Designers/agents propose. Showroom managers record actual completion.

questions.question: What are approved fixture sizes, thickness/load limits and travel envelopes?
questions.proposed_answer: Supply versioned supplier CAD/GLB and dimensioned constraints, including 6/9/12 mm compatibility.

questions.question: Which routes, services, sightlines and fixed anchors must remain clear?
questions.proposed_answer: Mark verified keep-outs and minimum clearances on the APS plan. Current map limits are draft.

questions.question: What defines Anatolia identity in a live room or display run?
questions.proposed_answer: Provide three approved and three rejected examples covering density, color balance, lighting and furniture.

questions.question: Who orders, prepares, moves and verifies each item, and what proves completion?
questions.proposed_answer: Use a role-owned task with receipt/preparation/installation evidence and disposition of removed material.
